title: Site Reliability Engineer, Hardware
description:
Brief info about Vinted 

Our mission is to make second-hand the first choice, and we're looking for people who want to help us get there. Every day, we work together to help our members buy and sell pre-loved clothing and lifestyle items, giving each piece a second life - or even a third.
The Vinted Group is made up of three business units that support this mission:

Vinted Marketplace is Europe’s leading platform for second-hand fashion and a go-to destination for all kinds of pre-loved items, with a growing range of categories. Our platform connects millions of members across 20+ markets, helping great items find a new life.

Vinted Go enhances the shipping experience with a vast network of over 500,000 pick-up and drop-off points, partnering with more than 60 carriers across Europe, with added services like item verification for peace of mind on high-value pieces.

Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.

Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people. 

Information about the position 

As a Site Reliability Engineer on the Hardware team, you’ll be responsible for maintaining 10,000+ servers across Vinted’s data centers.

You’ll help monitor and debug production servers to ensure we meet our established SLOs. This will involve diving deep into hardware configuration, BIOS, BMC, and Linux systems to identify bugs, troubleshoot issues, and test performance. You’ll also automate server provisioning, build Grafana dashboards, and set up monitoring alerts.

You’ll work closely with data center administrators, who handle physical server repairs, helping them identify issues and validate fixes after repairs are completed. You’ll also collaborate with other teams to support them with hardware - and software-related challenges.

In this position, you’ll 

• Lead data center infrastructure reliability initiatives across 10,000+ physical servers.

• Build up automation tooling for server provisioning, configuration management, testing, and large-scale deployments.

• Create scripts, tools, and workflows to reduce manual operational work and improve infrastructure efficiency.

• Assist with troubleshooting hardware, BIOS, BMC, Redfish, Linux OS, networking, and performance-related issues.

• Communicate with infrastructure, platform, and engineering teams to support secure, scalable, and performant services.

• Participate in production incident response, root cause analysis, and on-call rotation.

• Monitor data center infrastructure, server health, SLOs, Grafana dashboards, alerts, and production systems.

• Oversee testing and benchmarking of new server hardware, CPU, and GPU models.

• Keep track of data center assets, hardware configurations, and infrastructure documentation in DCIM/NetBox.

• Work with the Platform Foundations DC team to create reliable, automated, and scalable infrastructure solutions.

• Maintain configuration-as-code repositories and automated tests.

• Improve server provisioning and configurations.

• Support other engineering teams who are running their services on servers.

• Collaborate with engineers to identify infrastructure bottlenecks and implement long-term improvements.

About you 

• Have experience with large-scale physical servers infrastructure and linux operating systems.

• Have a strong understanding of hardware automation and monitoring.

• Care deeply about scalability and production stability. 

• Excellent written and spoken English

• Comfortable with production troubleshooting, debugging, and participation

description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril's Air & Missile Defense Radar team develops cutting-edge tracking algorithms and software systems that detect, track, and characterize airborne threats in real-time. Working in small, focused teams, our software engineers design and implement sophisticated tracking solutions that protect lives and critical assets. Our work spans the full spectrum-from developing novel multi-target tracking algorithms to building high-performance distributed systems that process massive amounts of sensor data in milliseconds

We don't just publish papers; we deploy production-grade systems that our government and industry customers depend on for mission-critical operations. If you're passionate about applying mathematics, software engineering, and signal processing to solve complex real-world problems, we want to hear from you.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

• Design and implement advanced tracking algorithms for novel air and missile threats, including multi-target tracking, track fusion, and discrimination techniques

• Develop high-performance, real-time software systems that process radar sensor data and maintain tracks on dozens to hundreds of simultaneous targets

• Build and leverage modeling & simulation environments to validate tracking performance, quantify system capabilities, and identify areas for improvement

• Collaborate directly with radar engineers and system architects to integrate tracking solutions into end-to-end defense systems

• Optimize tracking software for performance-critical environments where milliseconds matter

• Communicate technical concepts and trade-offs to cross-functional teams, program leadership, and customers to drive informed decisions

• Participate in customer demonstrations and field tests to ensure successful deployment and operational effectiveness

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• 2 years of relevant experience & Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Physics, or related technical field (or equivalent experience)

• Strong programming skills in C++ and Python

• Solid foundation in mathematics: linear algebra, probability, statistics, and/or differential equations

• Understanding of software engineering fundamentals: design patterns, testing, version control, and debugging

• Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Top Secret SCI security clearance

DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Experience with tracking, estimation, or filtering algorithms (Kalman filters, particle filters, multiple hypothesis tracking, etc.)

• Background in controls, estimation theory, or digital signal processing

• Familiarity with radar systems or sensor fusion

• Experience with high-performance computing (multithreading, GPU acceleration, distributed systems)

• Knowledge of machine learning techniques for classification, clustering, or data association

• Proficiency with database technologies (SQL, NoSQL, time-series databases)

• Experience with web development technologies (JavaScript, React, Node.js) for building visualization and analysis tools

• Familiarity with modeling and simulation tools (MATLAB, Simulink, or custom frameworks)

• Experience working in agile development environments

• Active U.S. Top Secret SCI clearance

title: Bookkeeper
description:
This is a remote position.
About the Firm
Our client is a well-established wealth management firm with a robust in-house tax practice, built through the acquisition of a large CPA firm and supported by its sister company. The firm is seeking an experienced Bookkeeper to join their professional team.
This position is ideal for a hands-on accounting professional who thrives in a production-focused environment and enjoys managing multiple client engagements with precision and autonomy.
About the Role
The Bookkeeper plays a critical role in managing the firm’s monthly client accounting engagements from start to finish. The ideal candidate is highly detail-oriented, comfortable managing multiple deadlines, and confident working within QuickBooks Desktop and QuickBooks Online at a power-user level.
This role is also a proven growth path into our Staff Accountant position for bookkeepers who want to expand into fuller-cycle accounting and, eventually, tax-adjacent work.
Key Responsibilities

• Manage a portfolio of monthly bookkeeping clients (up to 15-20 at capacity over time).

• Take each client engagement from start to finish on a monthly basis.

• Perform full-cycle bookkeeping, including transaction coding, bank and credit card reconciliations, and general ledger maintenance.

• Prepare and finalize monthly financial statements.

• Review work and ensure accuracy of account classifications and reporting.

• Communicate with clients to gather necessary documentation and clarify transactions (initially limited client-facing responsibility, with opportunity to grow into a more client-facing role over time).

• Maintain organized and accurate financial records in compliance with firm standards and accounting best practices.

• Utilize QuickBooks Desktop and QuickBooks Online extensively as a power user.

Requirements

• 5+ years of bookkeeping experience, preferably within a public accounting environment (candidates with 8-10+ years are encouraged to apply).

• Strong understanding of full-cycle bookkeeping, account reconciliations, journal entries, and financial statement preparation.

• Advanced proficiency in QuickBooks Desktop and QuickBooks Online required.

• Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple client deadlines.

• Ability to step into the role with minimal training and operate independently - while still receiving mentorship and support from the team.

• Located in Eastern or Central time zone.

Benefits

• Compensation:Competitive compensation commensurate with experience.

• Work arrangement:Remote or hybrid, depending on proximity to a firm office.

•Paid Time Off:Flexible/unlimited PTO.
•Retirement:401(k) with company match.

• Health coverage:Medical, dental, and vision insurance.

title: Senior Product Manager - Special Projects
description:
Tremendous is the global platform built for businesses to send thousands of payouts to anyone, anywhere, for free. We're trusted by 20,000 organizations like Atlassian, MIT, and United Way to deliver gift cards and money to millions of recipients worldwide.

Our customers (researchers, marketers, HR teams, nonprofits, and platform businesses) rave about how fast and easy Tremendous is to use. Check out our ratings on G2 https://www.g2.com/products/tremendous/reviews.

Tremendous is profitable and growing without outside investors. We’re a fully remote, high-documentation, low-meeting culture, which means more time for what matters in both your professional and personal life. The team agrees- our employee NPS is in the high 80s.

About the role

Most PMs at Tremendous run a squad. This role owns problems instead.

We're growing fast and spinning up new product areas. Each one needs research, a roadmap, and shovel-ready specs before we staff it. That's your job. You'll dig into areas where we might launch a squad, and run projects too small to need one.

You'll carry one or two projects at a time, drawn from the company's highest-priority open questions. When a problem proves worth solving, what happens next depends on how big the opportunity is.

If it justifies a long-term team, you'll likely build that squad and lead it as its PM. If it's worth building but smaller, you'll build it yourself with an engineer or two and design help from a related squad. If it's small and close to an existing squad's work, you'll hand it off with a finished brief, and that squad's PM will carry it forward. You'll have real influence over new project areas and which teams exist a year from now.

Today, the product management org is 7 PMs, led by a co-founder who serves as Head of Product.

You will

- Report to our Co-founder / Head of Product, Kapil Kale https://www.linkedin.com/in/kapilvkale/

- Own new product areas before they have a team. Develop a thesis, do the research, size the opportunity, and make a recommendation: spin up a squad, build it lean, hand it off, or kill it. Kill calls are as valuable as green lights.

- Turn research into shovel-ready work. Your output is briefs, prototypes, and specs that a squad can pick up and build immediately.

- Move quickly using AI. Use agents to dig through customer tickets, sales calls, usage data, and competitor research. Ship clickable prototypes in days to test ideas with real customers.

- Run projects that don't need a full squad. Some work is worth doing but too small for a team. You'll drive these end-to-end with engineers from existing squads.

- Cover a squad when needed. If a team is temporarily without a PM, you may step in. This is occasional, and your portfolio comes first.

- Work async. Most product work here happens in writing. If you're used to running product through meetings, this will feel different.

You have

- 6+ years building and shipping web applications as a designer, engineer, or product manager at tech companies, with at least 2 years taking new products from zero to one.

- Comfortable being the only person accountable for an initiative that doesn't have a team yet.

- Comfortable owning a portfolio instead of a single product. If validation kills your thesis, you move to the next bet without drama.

- A track record of turning ambiguous opportunities into prioritized, shovel-ready roadmaps.

- Strong product intuition, design judgment, and technical fluency. You hold your own with designers and engineers.

- Outstanding written communication. We're documentation-first, and this role runs on briefs and decision memos that need to persuade senior stakeholders.

- Founder, founding PM, or first-product-hire experience is a strong plus.

What’s cool about the role

- Competitive pay and equity. Base salary for this role: $250,000 to $325,000.

- Real benefits. 100% covered health (US), unlimited PTO, 12-16 weeks paid parental leave.

- Fully remote. Work from anywhere

title: Conducteur / Collecteur de données à Rignac, France
description:
Description de l'entreprise 
Terry Soot Management Group (TSMG) est une entreprise spécialisée dans la collecte de données sur le terrain, fondée en 2017 en Europe. Nous collectons des données là où l’automatisation est impossible. Nous comptons les caractéristiques, prenons des photos, réalisons des vidéos, enregistrons des voix et scannons des zones pour vous fournir tous les détails nécessaires à une prise de décision éclairée. Nos équipes de collecte de données sur le terrain sont réparties à travers l’Europe et l’Amérique du Nord, prêtes à accepter de nouveaux défis. 
 
Objectif du projet
L'objectif du projet est de collecter des images de haute qualité de rues, de points d’intérêt clés et d’espaces publics dans tous les pays de l’UE. À l’aide de véhicules équipés de caméras amovibles à 360° et de lidars, les conducteurs captureront des images complètes des environs. Les données collectées seront stockées sur des ordinateurs de bord (disques SSD) et utilisées plus tard pour améliorer l'une des cartes en ligne les plus populaires au monde.
Les collecteurs de données suivent des itinéraires prédéfinis, en se concentrant sur les rues publiques, les zones commerciales et les points d’intérêt. Pour assurer la meilleure qualité d’image, certaines zones devront être revisitées lors de conditions météorologiques favorables.
La durée du projet varie en fonction de l’étendue des travaux requis dans chaque zone ciblé de collecte de données. En moyenne, les missions impliquent de 3 à 6 mois de travail actif.
 
Horaire de travail: engagement à temps plein dans les heures normales d’ouverture (de 8 h - à 19 h)
Le processus de recrutement pour le poste de conducteur comprend les étapes suivantes : un test de conduite sécuritaire, un entretien avec un recruteur et un processus d’intégration.

As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril designs and fields systems across an unusually broad materials portfolio, and the design decisions behind them depend on mechanical test data that is accurate, repeatable, and delivered on time. This role owns the execution of that testing.

This is your opportunity to be the person who makes the materials lab run - turning a growing set of capital equipment into dependable throughput, taking routine testing off engineers’ plates, and setting the standard for how mechanical testing gets done. You’ll own the bench, not just a task on it.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Run Mechanical Testing. Execute tensile, compression, and other mechanical tests to established methods (e.g., ASTM / ISO) across programs - set up fixturing, operate the load frame, and capture results accurately.

• You take pride in doing hands-on work precisely and repeatably. A test run to method and data you can stand behind is its own reward.

• You have a bias for action and ownership. You keep the queue moving and don’t wait to be asked.

• You communicate clearly with the engineers you support, surfacing anomalies rather than burying them.

• You care about a safe, orderly lab and treat the equipment like it’s your own.

• Associate degree in a technical field, or equivalent hands-on experience in a materials, mechanical, or manufacturing test environment

• 3+ years of hands-on experience operating mechanical test equipment (servo-hydraulic or electromechanical load frames)

• Careful data-capture and record-keeping habits, with strong attention to traceability

• Ability to manage a queue of work and shifting priorities independently in a fast-paced environment

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

We believe patients living with kidney disease deserve the best care. We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.

- Extreme ownership. Full autonomy. Own things end to end often taking on scope outside your core role without being asked to get things done.

- Velocity. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

THE MODULAR TEAM

The Modular team is building factory-produced modular data centers, taking them from released drawings to rate production on our Phoenix manufacturing line.

- Bring first-of-a-kind modular data center designs from engineering release to repeatable rate production on the factory line

title: Enablement Lead, Government
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Adoption, Innovation, and Transformation team within OpenAI for Government helps government organizations turn OpenAI products into durable capabilities and measurable mission impact.

We work alongside public servants to move from initial exploration to confident, responsible, organization-wide use of AI. Our work combines hands-on enablement, adoption strategy, deployment support, community, content, and practical transformation tailored to government missions and operating environments.

By translating the potential of OpenAI’s technology into better individual workflows, stronger teams, and improved public services, we help government customers deepen adoption, build lasting organizational capability, and spend more time on mission.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Enablement Lead, Government is a specialist role focused on delivering high-impact enablement and adoption services across OpenAI’s product suite. This role is responsible for designing and delivering experiences that support repeatable adoption frameworks, drive sustained activation, expand the breadth and depth of usage, and produce measurable value for government organizations.

This role sits at the intersection of enablement, education, adoption, community, content, and customer experience. It blends strong product fluency, instructional design, customer advisory, and a deep understanding of public service. You will lead live workshops, deliver enablement programs, and design adoption interventions for audiences ranging from front-line public servants and technical practitioners to senior government leaders.

You will be a trusted guide to government customers, helping them learn, share, teach, celebrate successes, and use AI confidently in their day-to-day work. You will help organizations understand not only what OpenAI’s products can do, but how to apply them safely and effectively while respecting their missions, operating environments, workforce needs, and responsibilities to the public.

Success in this role means accelerating customer confidence, increasing product adoption, supporting successful launches and deployments, and helping government organizations translate product capabilities into tangible mission outcomes. You will own outcomes related to activation and sustained usage while helping shape how OpenAI enables and supports public-sector customers at scale.

This role is based in San Francisco or Washington, D.C. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. Travel and regular work from government customer sites are required.

IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

- Own the enablement of OpenAI products, including ChatGPT Enterprise and Agents, helping define effective patterns for responsible adoption across government organizations.

- Lead government customers through the full enablement lifecycle, from initial onboarding and activation through expansion, optimization, and long-term adoption.

- Define and manage structured enablement and deployment programs with clear goals, milestones, owners, and measures of success.

- Design and deliver high-impact engagements-including onboarding sessions, advanced capability training, executive briefings, academies, hackathons, listening sessions, and hands-on mission or workflow labs-for audiences ranging from senior leaders to front-line staff.

- Guide government leaders, champions, technical teams, and working teams through organizational change by building confidence, establishing effective habits, and translating product capabilities into practical workflows and mission outcomes.

- Serve as a subject matter expert for designated products, roles, or government mission areas, building deep expertise and identifying emerging public-sector use cases for new product capabilities.

- Develop government-specific learning journeys, training materials, playbooks, FAQs, demonstrations, use cases, customer impact stories, and communication

title: Supply Chain Delivery Manager, Data Center Power & Cooling OFE
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

•
About the Role

Anthropic is bringing data center capacity online faster than the industry has ever attempted, and the owner-furnished equipment (OFE) that makes a site live - switchgear, transformers, UPS, generators, busway, PDUs, chillers, CDUs, air handlers, dry coolers, pumps and piping skids - is long-lead, high-value, and sits squarely on the construction critical path. When a transformer slips three weeks at the factory, a data hall slips three weeks at the site.

We're hiring a Supply Chain Delivery Manager to own that equipment from purchase order to dock. You will be the site-facing supply chain lead for a regional portfolio of data center projects: tracking every OFE line item against the construction schedule, running factory and logistics escalations with OEMs, holding suppliers and general contractors accountable for delivery performance, and giving leadership a clear, converged picture of delivery risk across the portfolio. Your job is to make sure equipment production and delivery are never the reason a site misses its ready-for-service date.

This is a senior individual-contributor role on the Compute DC Infrastructure team, working daily with Construction, Electrical and Mechanical Engineering, Strategic Sourcing, Commissioning, and our general contractors and OEMs. It is not a category-management or negotiation role - Sourcing owns supplier strategy and commercial terms - and it is not a people-management role. The emphasis is execution: schedules, escalations, logistics, and site readiness.

What You'll Do

Delivery planning and schedule integration

•
Own the end-to-end OFE delivery plan for each site in your portfolio: order placement, engineering submittal/approval milestones, production slots, FAT dates, ship dates, and required-on-site (ROS) dates, integrated with the GC's construction schedule.

•
Engage during preconstruction with Construction, Engineering, and the GC to set OFE delivery expectations, sequence equipment arrivals to the build, and identify schedule risk before POs are cut.

•
Lead OFE kickoff meetings at the site level with the GC and internal construction teams, establishing points of contact, delivery windows, receiving requirements, and escalation paths.

•
Maintain the single source of truth for OFE status across the portfolio - a live tracker of every line item, its milestone dates, and its risk rating.

Supplier execution and escalation

•
Run weekly delivery cadences with OEMs and integrators on open orders; verify production progress against committed slots rather than accepting reported dates at face value.

•
Act as the primary escalation point for factory slips, component shortages, FAT failures, and shipping delays; drive recovery plans (expedites, partial ships, resequencing, alternate sources) with Sourcing and Engineering.

•
Partner with Sourcing on corporate-level supplier escalations, bringing site-level schedule intelligence to commercial conversations.

•
Hold GC OFCI teams accountable for receiving, storage, and installation-readiness performance; manage the change/claim process when delivery issues affect the GC's schedule.

Logistics and site readiness

•
Plan and coordinate transportation for oversize/overweight and high-value equipment - carrier selection, route surveys, permits, crane and rigging coordination - with our logistics partners and the GC.

•
Manage laydown, staging, and interim storage decisions when site readiness and equipment arrival diverge; coordinate with Quality and Commissioning on receiving inspection and storage/preservation requirements.

•
Ensure equipment arrives complete - accessories, spares, doc

The Commercial Systems and Intelligence squad is a newly formed team within SumUp's Acquisition Mission under the Run & Grow tribe. title: Senior Estimator – Civil / Road Infrastructure
description:
ABOUT THE COMPANY

Our client is an Australian business supplying road safety barriers - for roadsides, car parks, schools and other sites - to councils, contractors and construction clients across Australia. The business is led by its General Manager and Operations Manager, who this role reports to directly.

PRIMARY PURPOSE

To independently run the day-to-day estimating and quoting workflow - checking plans against the schedule, taking off quantities, sourcing supplier pricing and working out margins - and to build the kind of trust with management, through accurate work, honest communication and a focus on keeping the client happy, that lets the role take on more of the client-facing side over time.

ABOUT THE ROLE

• A senior, full-time Estimator role at the centre of the quoting process - reviewing customer enquiries, checking supplied plans against the job schedule, and turning that into an accurate, priced quote using the company's own templates and rates.

• Internally, one person currently runs estimating end to end, from enquiry through to submitting the quote to the client. Remotely, this role owns the estimating and quoting engine room - checking plans, sourcing supplier pricing, working out margins and building the quote - while management keeps final client sign-off and quote submission in-house at the start.

• As trust builds over the first few months, there is scope for this role to take on more direct client contact. This is not a sales role, and no commercial decision is made without management's sign-off.

• Trusted to work independently on the estimating and quoting workflow and exercise judgement on scope and pricing questions within agreed rates - but genuinely understanding an instruction, plan or piece of feedback, and asking a clarifying question rather than guessing or agreeing by default, matters more in this role than in most.

• Keeping the client happy sits behind every part of this role - even while quote submission stays with management at the start, the accuracy, turnaround and professionalism of the work behind the scenes is what keeps the client relationship strong.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

▸ Enquiries & Plan Review

• Review new customer enquiries and the plans or drawings supplied for the job

• Check the supplied plans against the job schedule to confirm they match, and flag any differences before quoting rather than assuming

• Request missing photos, information or clarification from management rather than guessing

▸ Takeoffs & Quote Preparation

• Perform takeoffs from civil/road design drawings using Adobe for markup and measurement

• Record and tally quantities in Excel, and build the quote using the company's templates, pricing structure and rates

• Own quote accuracy and turnaround time on the estimating side, with minimal supervision

▸ Pricing & Supplier Coordination

• Source and compare pricing from a couple of different suppliers for each job

• Chase, confirm and follow up outstanding supplier pricing

• Work out margins and the final cost to the business before the quote goes to management

▸ Client Communication (Phased)

• In the early months, prepare the quote for management to review and issue to the client directly - client-facing communication and quote submission stay in-house at the start

• Communicate with suppliers directly as required, using the company's official email

• Flag anything a client mentions that could be a new opportunity back to management, even though this is not a sales role

• Over time, and only as agreed with management, take on more direct client contact - by email first, and potentially by phone later

▸ Communication & Judgement

• Ask a clarifying question rather than guessing or agreeing to an instruction, plan or piece of feedback that isn't fully understood - the single most important trait for this role

• Communicate clearly and accurately in written and spoken English with management and suppliers

• Escalate only genuine exception

title: Senior Physical Design Engineer - P&R
description:
About BTA Design Services

Headquartered in Ottawa, BTA Design Services supports the electronic design community across Canada and internationally, specializing in ASIC and FPGA design, verification, and embedded software development. We strengthen our clients' engineering teams and accelerate the delivery of complete, production ready designs.

We are adaptable, efficient, and built around exceptional technical talent. Our continued growth reflects the trust our clients place in us, and we are currently searching globally for a Senior Physical Design Engineer with deep expertise in place and route.
About the Engagement
You will join BTA Design Services as an employee and work on behalf of one of our clients, an industry leader building advanced silicon platforms for next generation AI infrastructure. The work pairs leading edge CMOS design with the bandwidth and power demands of modern AI, and the client partners with the world's foremost foundries to bring frontier designs to production. Further details are shared with candidates under confidentiality during the interview process.

This engagement places you at the center of that work, delivering world-class ASICs on the most demanding technology nodes in the industry.
About the Position
As a Senior Physical Design Engineer, you will own backend implementation from netlist to GDSII on challenging blocks and sub-systems. You will apply advanced flows and techniques on single-digit FinFET technology nodes, working alongside a strong and experienced team to bring complex designs to closure. This is a senior, fully remote role, and you may be located anywhere.
Key Responsibilities

• Run place and route implementation flows and analyze the results.

• Create effective floorplans that support physically aware synthesis.

• Drive designs to timing closure and run physical verification.

• Debug issues spanning tools, timing constraints, DFT, and design.

• Partner with the design team to improve RTL and make it implementation friendly.

• Implement and apply timing ECOs.

• Run PrimeTime and analyze timing reports.

• Develop strategies to optimize power and area.

• Run IR-drop analysis and identify optimal strategies to improve it.

• Interface with analog and front-end teams to align on shared objectives.

Key Qualifications

• 8 or more years of relevant experience in ASIC digital place and route.

• Recent, hands-on experience with leading EDA tools and advanced flows (Synopsys and Cadence).

• Strong understanding of advanced FinFET technology nodes, DRC rules, and node-specific P&R requirements.

• Practical experience with floorplanning.

• Solid grasp of CTS concepts and the ability to design clocks to meet timing requirements.

• Working knowledge of IR-drop optimization strategies.

• Experience with timing closure and ECO implementation (PT-ECO or Tweaker experience is an asset).

• Strong scripting skills.

• Exposure to several of the following: synthesis, StarRC, PT DMSA, RedHawk, Calibre, and formal verification (LEC or Formality).

• A track record as a self-starter who also works well within a team.

Remote Work
This role is fully remote and open to candidates in any location. You will collaborate with distributed engineering teams across time zones, so strong written communication, self-direction, and the discipline to deliver independently are essential.
Why Work With Us
We offer challenging, stimulating technical work with companies that lead the world in technology and innovation. At BTA Design Services , we know our strength lies in the people who join us, so we foster an environment where everyone is trusted, valued, and engaged. We also believe work-life balance matters, and we give our engineers demanding, rewarding roles while leaving room for family, friends, and life beyond work. This is a new position. Only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

Disclaimer
BTA Design Services is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications

title: Junior Budget Execution Analyst (Supporting NOAA)
description:
ASRC Federal is a leading government contractor furthering missions in space, public health and defense. As an Alaska Native owned corporation, our work helps secure an enduring future for our shareholders. Join our team and discover why we are a top veteran employer and Certified Great Place to Work™
ASRC Federal Advanced Research (AFAR), a subsidiary of ASRC Federal Holding Company, is currently recruiting for a remote Junior Budget Execution Analyst to support a federal government client located in Silver Spring, MD. Work hours for this position are aligned to the Eastern Time Zone.
Key Role:
The successful candidate will provide budget planning and budget execution support for the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA)/National Weather Service (NWS) client. The candidate will assist in creating and maintaining the spreadsheets, tools, forms, templates, and instructions to support various monthly and quarterly reports and meetings. They will work with various branches to ensure that the new and existing financial processes are understood and implemented correctly. Integral to the role is the ability to analyze data to understand trends, forecast potential budget issues, and to plan and take corrective actions. The candidate will track NWS grants and contracts as they move through planning, funding, and execution. Finally, they will provide analyses, assessments, and recommendations relating to financial management activities, among other duties as assigned.
This is a remote position. The duties for this role include, but are not limited to:

• Provide budget execution support to a NWS Financial Management Center (FMC) or Headquarters.

• Become adept at pulling reports from the NOAA financial systems, including the Oracle E-Business Suite (EBS), Enterprise Data Warehouse (EDW), and the Financial Management Data System (FMDS)

• Summarize quantitative data for monthly commitment, obligation, and contract status reports as well as a variety of complex payment reports

• Assist with creating and monitoring monthly and annual obligation plans.

• Track funds transferred in from other NOAA or NWS Financial Management Centers

• Understand the various types of accounting codes (i.e., program, project, and tasks codes) being used and the business rules that govern them.

• Process documentation for financial corrections.

• Conduct variance analysis by comparing planned obligations to actual obligations; justify the reason behind variances to FMC leadership and NOAA headquarters.

• Create and utilize tracking tools to monitor NWS contracts and grants as they move through planning, clearance, funding, and execution.

• Transform accounting system data into Excel spreadsheets and PowerPoint presentations.

• Produce, maintain, and update templates, forms, process documents, and slides for NWS reviews.

• Respond to data calls from other FMCs, NWS Headquarters, NOAA Headquarters, the Department of Commerce, the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) and/or Congress.

• Enter data, as requested, into the Financial Management Data System.

Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s Degree plus 2 years of experience in federal budgeting or related industries (e.g., finance, budgeting, accounting or other highly quantitative field). 4 years of relevant experience may be used as a substitute for a bachelor's degree. • Excellent oral presentation skills with the ability to brief findings and materials to management.
